# std.broadcast

<!-- Generated by `badger doc std` from the checked interfaces (badger 0.1.0). Do not edit by hand. -->

Broadcast: every subscriber receives each message published after it
subscribed (unlike a channel, where each message has one consumer).

Retention is per subscriber: a bounded backlog of `backlog` messages.
When a subscriber's backlog is full, the policy decides:
- `:drop_oldest` (default): the oldest pending message is dropped and the
  subscriber's `lagged()` count grows; publishing never waits.
- `:block`: publishing waits for the slow subscriber.

A subscriber that is done calls `close()`: publishing then stops
delivering to it (and, under `:block`, stops waiting for it). One that is
only dropped stays subscribed, since the broadcaster still holds its end.

## Types

### `Broadcaster`

```badger
struct Broadcaster<T> { subs: Atom<List<{id: Int, sender: channel.Sender<T>, receiver: channel.Receiver<T>, lagged: Atom<Int>}>>, next_id: Atom<Int>, backlog: Int, blocking: Bool, closed: Atom<Bool> }
```

#### `Broadcaster.close`

```badger
fn close(self: &Self) -> Unit !{State}
```

End the broadcast: subscribers drain what they have, then see `none`.

#### `Broadcaster.publish`

```badger
fn publish(self: &Self, value: T) -> Int !{Wait, State}
```

Deliver `value` to every current subscriber (per the retention
policy). Returns the number of subscribers reached.

#### `Broadcaster.subscribe`

```badger
fn subscribe(self: &Self) -> Result<Subscription<T>, Error> !{State}
```

Receive every message published from now on.

#### `Broadcaster.subscribers`

```badger
fn subscribers(self: &Self) -> Int !{State}
```

### `Error`

```badger
pub type Error = channel.ConfigError
```

### `Options`

```badger
pub type Options = { backlog: Int, policy: Symbol }
```

### `Subscription`

```badger
struct Subscription<T> { receiver: channel.Receiver<T>, lagged: Atom<Int> }
```

#### `Subscription.close`

```badger
fn close(self: &Self) -> Unit
```

Stop receiving: later publishes skip this subscriber (and stop
waiting for it).

#### `Subscription.lagged`

```badger
fn lagged(self: &Self) -> Int !{State}
```

Messages dropped because this subscriber fell behind.

#### `Subscription.recv`

```badger
fn recv(self: &Self) -> Option<T> !{Wait}
```

The next message, or `none` after the broadcast closed and drained.
